```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea B is a defined product with a defined payer: micro-SaaS sellers listing and selling startups. Idea A's own source marks the concept as unconfirmed ('one-line description to confirm') and the customer as 'varies by idea'. A product with no fixed shape is hard to sell to a paying customer within 90 days.",
    "Idea B has a proven payment model across five live competitors with published pricing. Acquire.com charges $25-100/mo to list plus a 6-8% closing fee, and Flippa charges $29+ to list plus a 5-10% success fee. Upfront listing fees offer a path to a first paying seller before any deal closes, which matters for a 90-day target.",
    "Idea A has no priced direct competitor. Foundry, People.Build and Nixbly are free, pre-revenue, and in two cases show dummy or illustrative data. The only price anchor, CoFoundersLab at $29/mo, sits in an adjacent category and carries a billing class-action caveat.",
    "Idea B's demand evidence comes from both sides of the market. One seller says they could not find buyers. One operator reports 500+ daily visitors and about 30 listings two weeks after launch. Idea A's demand evidence is a single vague post, and the same thread rebuts it.",
    "Idea A faces a structural threat that the brief itself documents: AI vibe-coding tools let non-coders build their own prototypes, which removes the core need for friends or builders to do it for them. Idea B's risks are serious, including buyer-side liquidity, 0%-commission rivals, and a $750 newsletter test that produced zero sales. Those risks fall on growth and profitability. They do not rule out getting one paying customer.",
    "Idea B also maps its regulatory setup (third-party escrow, broker-licensing check). This shows the operational path has been looked at, and Idea A's brief has no equivalent."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence is one vague Reddit post ('Looking for someone to make apps with lmk...') retrieved from a third-party mirror snapshot rather than the original thread. The same thread contains a direct rebuttal to the premise ('you can just vibe code if you have an idea'). This is the only demand signal in the brief, and it shows no willingness to pay. A secondary weakness is the $100-200 CAC estimate, which comes from a vendor blog the brief itself labels 'not independently verified'.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-high confidence that B is the better first bet. Idea A's brief undermines itself: the concept is undefined, competitors show no traction, and AI tools erode the need. B is still a hard bet. It is a crowded two-sided marketplace where cheaper and free alternatives already exist, and the brief documents buyer-conversion weakness and a failed paid-acquisition test. Reaching a first paying customer in 90 days likely depends on charging sellers upfront for listings or services, or on taking a narrow wedge such as an AI buyer-matching or curated-dealflow layer. Waiting on closing fees from a cold buyer pool is unlikely to get there in time."
}
```
